text:
For the following reactions

$A⟶^{700K}\mathrm{Product}$

$A⟶_{catalyst}^{500K}\mathrm{Product}$

it was found that $E_{a}$ is decreased by 30 kJ/mol
in the presence of catalyst.

If the rate remains unchanged, the activation
energy for catalysed reaction is (Assume pre
exponential factor is same):
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$K_{1} = Ae^{-\frac{Ea}{R\times 700}}$

$K_{2} = Ae^{-\frac{(Ea-30)}{R\times 500}}$

$\because$Rate is same

$\therefore$ Rate constant will also be same

$K_{1} = K_{2}$

A$e^{-\frac{Ea}{R\times 700}}$ = A$e^{-\frac{(Ea-30)}{R\times 500}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{(E_{a}-30)}{R\times 500}$ = $\frac{E_{a}}{R\times 700}$

$\Rightarrow$ $5E_{a} = 7E_{a} – 210$

$\Rightarrow$ $210 = 2E_{a}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E_{a} = 105 kJ/$mole

$\therefore$ Activation energy in the presence of
catalyst = 105 – 30 = 75 kJ/mol

text:
[Pd(F)(Cl)(Br)(I)]$^{2–}$ has n number of
geometrical isomers. Then, the spin-only
magnetic moment and crystal field stabilisation
energy [CFSE] of [$Fe(CN)_{6}$]$^{n–6}$, respectively,
are:

[Note : Ignore the pairing energy]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{F})(\mathrm{Cl})(\mathrm{Br})(\mathrm{I})]{}^{2-}$ is a square planar $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$ complex, which has 3 geometrical isomers, so $n=3$ and the second complex is $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$.

In $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$, iron is $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ with the configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}$.

$\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ is a strong-field ligand, and with the pairing energy ignored nothing opposes pairing, so all five electrons enter the $t_{2g}$ set: $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, with 1 unpaired electron.

$μ=\sqrt{1(1+2)}=\sqrt{3}=1.73\text{BM}$

Ignoring the pairing energy, the CFSE contains only the $\Delta _{0}$ terms:

$\text{CFSE}=(-0.4\times 5+0.6\times 0)\Delta _{0}=-2.0\Delta _{0}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

If the magnetic moment of a dioxygen species
is 1.73 B.M, it may be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Magnetic moment = 1.73 BM

$\therefore$ Unpaired electron = 1

(1) $O_{2}$ has 16 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $O_{2}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

Here 2 unpaired electron present.

(2)   $O_{2}^{+}$ has 15 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{+}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{0}}^{\ast }$

Here 1 unpaired electron present.

(3)   $O_{2}^{-}$ has 17 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{-}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

Here 1 unpaired electron present.

Hence $O_{2}^{-}$ & $O_{2}^{+}$
 have one unpaired electron.

text:
B has a smaller first ionization enthalpy than
Be. Consider the following statements :

(I) It is easier to remove 2p electron than 2s
electron

(II) 2p electron of B is more shielded from the
nucleus by the inner core of electrons than
the 2s electrons of Be.

(III) 2s electron has more penetration power
than 2p electron.

(IV) atomic radius of B is more than Be
(Atomic number B = 5, Be = 4)

The correct statements are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the first ionization, Be ($1s^{2}2s^{2}$) loses a $2s$ electron while B ($1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{1}$) loses a $2p$ electron.

A $2s$ electron penetrates closer to the nucleus than a $2p$ electron, so statement (III) is correct.

Owing to its lower penetration, the $2p$ electron of B is more effectively shielded from the nucleus by the inner core of electrons than the $2s$ electrons of Be, so statement (II) is correct.

The $2p$ electron of B therefore feels a smaller effective nuclear charge and is easier to remove than the $2s$ electron of Be, so statement (I) is correct; this is why $\Delta _{i}H_{1}$ of B is smaller than that of Be.

Atomic radius decreases across a period as the nuclear charge increases, so B (88 pm) is smaller than Be (111 pm) and statement (IV) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
Complex X of composition $Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}Cl_{n}$
has a spin only magnetic moment of 3.83
BM. It reacts with AgNO$_{3}$ and shows
geometrical isomerism. The IUPAC
nomenclature of X is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The spin-only magnetic moment is $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons. $μ=3.83$ BM gives $n=3$, since $\sqrt{3\times 5}=3.87$ BM.

Three unpaired electrons means a $3d^{3}$ ion, i.e. $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$, so the compound contains three chloride ions: $\mathrm{CrCl}{}_{3}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

Its hydrate isomers are $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}$, $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\cdot \mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}\cdot 2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}]\cdot 3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$. A precipitate with $\mathrm{AgNO}{}_{3}$ needs ionisable chloride, which rules out $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}]\cdot 3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$ (type $\mathrm{MA}{}_{6}$) and $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]{}^{2+}$ (type $\mathrm{MA}{}_{5}\mathrm{B}$) show no geometrical isomerism, while $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{+}$ (type $\mathrm{MA}{}_{4}\mathrm{B}{}_{2}$) has cis and trans forms.

So X is $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}\cdot 2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$. Ligands are named alphabetically (aqua before chlorido) and chromium is $+3$: tetraaquadichloridochromium(III) chloride dihydrate.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

The de Broglie wavelength of an electron in the
4th Bohr orbit is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

$r_{n}=\frac{n^{2}}{Z}\times a_{0}$

Also 2$πr_{n}$ = n$λ$

$\Rightarrow$ 2$π\frac{n^{2}}{Z}\times a_{0}$ = n$λ$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = $2π\times \frac{n}{Z}\times a_{0}$

For n = 4 and Z = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = 8$πa_{0}$

text:
108 g of silver (molar mass 108 g mol$^{–1})$ is
deposited at cathode from AgNO$_{3}(aq)$ solution
by a certain quantity of electricity. The
volume (in L) of oxygen gas produced at
273 K and 1 bar pressure from water by the
same quantity of electricity is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cathode : $Ag^{+}(aq) + e^{-}$ $\to$ Ag(s)

Moles of Ag deposited = $\frac{108}{108}$ = 1 mole

Anode : $2H_{2}O$ $\to$ $O_{2} + 4H^{+} + 4e^{-}$

Here we have to find volume of $O_{2}$ evolved.

Equivalence of Ag = Equivalence of $O_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 1 $\times$ $1 = n_{O2}$ $\times$ 4

$\Rightarrow$ $n_{O2} =$ $\frac{1}{4}$ mol

$\therefore$ Volume of $O_{2}$ evolved 

= $\frac{1}{4}$ $\times$ 22.4

= 5.6 lit
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
How much amount of NaCl should be added
to 600 g of water ($ρ$ = 1.00 g/mL) to decrease
the freezing point of water to – 0.2 °C ?
$______$. 

(The freezing point depression constant for water = 2K kg mol$^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\DeltaT_{f} = 0.2^{o} C$

$\therefore$ $\DeltaT_{f} = ik_{f}.m$

i = 2 for NaCl

$\therefore$ 0.2 = 2$\times$2$\times\frac{W_{NaCl}\times 1000}{58.5\times 600}$

$\Rightarrow$ $W_{$NaCl} = $\frac{58.5\times 600\times 0.2}{4\times 1000}$ = 1.76 g
